app_access.name: Review sign-in
app_access.instructions: On the sign-in screen, choose Link from another device: the phone or TV shows a code. In any browser, open https://api.usetortuga.app/review, enter the password from the sign-in details and the code, and choose Sign in the device. To see something play, open Settings, then Addons, choose Install addon, enter https://usetortuga.app/demo/manifest.json, then Continue and Install. On Home, in the Tortuga demo row, open Tears of Steel, choose Play and pick the Tortuga demo stream.

content_rating_iarc.category: All other app types (a media player; the app has no content of its own)
content_rating_iarc.users_interact_why: Watch together: people in a room see each other's profile names and what plays. No chat, voice or images.
content_rating_iarc.unrestricted_internet_why: Addons installed from any link supply catalogs, artwork and streams the app does not control.

data_safety.account_creation: OAuth (Sign in with Google, Apple, GitHub)
data_safety.shared_why: Nothing goes to a third party except at the user's request (addons they install, trackers they connect, watch-together rooms they open), which Play exempts from sharing. Crash reports go only to the developer's own crash-report server (self-hosted Bugs, an open-source error tracker).

collected.what: the sign-in provider's verified email, when it shares one
the provider's identifier for the user, the account ID, the username at a connected tracker

library, watch progress, watched marks, the stream picked for each video; while the profile's Suggest a stream setting is on (off by default), the streams picked by hand, each with the parsed descriptions of the streams shown around it (no links), the kind of device, whether the network was metered, what the screen and decoders handle and how playback went, to suggest a stream
profiles (name, avatar, PIN hash), each profile's addons with their links, profile settings
each signed-in device's session, with the device name and platform

collected.type: App info and performance: Crash logs
collected.what: when the app crashes (also in native code), stops responding, or a fault stops one part of it while the rest keeps running: the error, its stack trace and the app's events before it, with every link cut to its origin and no account or device ID; release builds only, on by default, off with Settings > This device > Privacy > Send crash reports

in each crash report: the app's version, the device's model, Android version, language and time zone, its memory, storage, battery and screen, and whether the app was in front; while the profile's Suggest a stream setting is on (off by default), with each stream picked by hand: the kind of device, what its screen and decoders handle, and whether the playback stalled or failed, to suggest a stream

not_collected: In-app search history (recent searches stay on the device)
